verses.text: When I came to you, brothers and sisters, I didn't come with impressive words or human wisdom as I announced God's truth.
I had decided to focus on nothing among you except Jesus Christ—and him crucified.
I came to you feeling weak, afraid, and deeply shaken.
My words and my preaching weren't clever or persuasive. They showed the Spirit's power,
so your faith wouldn't rest on human wisdom but on God's power.
We do speak wisdom among the mature, but it's not the wisdom of this age or its rulers, who are fading away.
We speak God's wisdom, a mystery once hidden, which God planned before the ages for our glory.
None of this age's rulers understood it. If they had, they wouldn't have crucified the Lord of glory.
But, as Scripture says, ‘What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined—this is what God has prepared for those who love him.’
God has revealed these things to us through the Spirit. The Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
Who knows a person's thoughts except that person's own spirit within them? In the same way, no one knows God's thoughts except God's Spirit.
We didn't receive the spirit of the world. We received the Spirit who comes from God, so we can understand the gifts God has freely given us.
We speak about these things, not with words taught by human wisdom, but with words taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual truths to spiritual people.
A person without the Spirit doesn't welcome the things that come from God's Spirit. They seem foolish, and that person can't understand them because they're spiritually discerned.
But the person who has the Spirit can discern all things, though no one can judge them.
As Scripture says, ‘Who has known the Lord's mind well enough to instruct him?’ But we have the mind of Christ.
